findings.evidence: Button label 'Subscribe' is dark grey/purple text on the violet gradient fill; visually close to the fill and well under 4.5:1 (estimated about 2.5:1 from the image).
findings.after: White label on a solid fill at 4.5:1 or better, checked at the darkest and lightest gradient stops (A11-166)

findings.where: light grey small text: 'TRUSTED BY FAST-MOVING TEAMS AT', logo names, footer column heads, footer tagline 'Product analytics for fast-moving teams.', copyright line
findings.evidence: Pale blue-grey on white at small sizes (about 12-13px caps for the labels); estimated around 2.5-3:1 from the image, and the logo names are a lighter grey still.
findings.before: light slate (approx. #94a3b8) small text on white
findings.after: Use a grey at 4.5:1 on white (e.g. #5b6577 or darker) for any text that must be read

findings.where: gradient text: 'just works' in h1 and the four stat figures
findings.evidence: Text filled with an indigo-to-pink gradient; the pink end on white and the lighter violet on the lavender stat band are the weakest stops and cannot be verified from an image.
findings.after: Solid text colour at 4.5:1 (3:1 for the large figures) against the band
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.3 / 1.4.11, measured at each gradient stop.

findings.where: newsletter email field border and secondary buttons ('Book a demo', 'Get started', 'Contact sales')
findings.evidence: Field and outline-button borders are a very light grey on white, visibly under 3:1, so the boundaries of the controls are hard to see.
Three emoji serve as the only visible label for social links; their names are emoji descriptions ('octopus', 'briefcase'), not the destination.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.4 Link Purpose and 1.1.1 Non-text Content (verify in code).

strengths: Body and heading text in dark slate on white is clearly legible at normal sizes.
not_investigated: image-only item: alt text, accessible names, focus order, keyboard, forms, reflow, landmarks and motion cannot be checked from a screenshot; only visible contrast, text size and colour use were judged
contrast values are estimates from pixels in the image, not measured from CSS
